allResults.question: A company wants repeatable promotion of an AI Builder model from development to production and clean servicing of later releases. Which approach should the architect recommend?
allResults.topic: D3.3 / Managed solution lifecycle for custom AI models
allResults.explanation: Microsoft recommends developing AI Builder models in a sandbox or development environment and deploying them to production with managed solutions. Imported-model edits are generally discouraged because they create unmanaged customizations. Keeping changes in source and promoting a new managed version preserves a repeatable, serviceable release path.

allResults.question: A Dynamics 365 Finance AI capability was validated in sandbox, but after the application update reaches production the intended users still cannot access it. What should the target-environment validation check?
allResults.topic: D3.3 / Dynamics 365 finance AI feature validation
allResults.explanation: The Finance and Operations Feature management workspace records whether a feature is off, on, scheduled, mandatory, requires attention, or unavailable in that environment. Microsoft also states that enabling a feature doesn't bypass security; users still need access through their security roles. Production validation must therefore cover both target feature state and authorization instead of treating package deployment as automatic enablement.

allResults.question: Customer Service Copilot works in test, but a newly provisioned production environment isn't ready for representatives. Which release checklist is most appropriate?
allResults.topic: D3.3 / Dynamics 365 Customer Service Copilot environment promotion
allResults.explanation: Customer Service Copilot is enabled by selecting and editing a specific environment in the Power Platform admin center. Microsoft lists System Administrator access and licensing prerequisites and documents region and data-movement conditions. A successful test release doesn't configure another environment, so production enablement and representative access require explicit target-environment validation.

allResults.question: A maker publishes an authenticated Copilot Studio agent and shares it with the entire finance department. A user can open the agent but cannot retrieve a restricted ledger record. The maker claims that sharing should grant access. Which security interpretation is correct?
allResults.explanation: Copilot Studio distinguishes access to the agent from authentication for tools and authorization in the underlying service. A secure design evaluates the author, runtime workload, end user, and source-system permission boundaries independently; neither publishing nor sharing transfers the maker's ledger privileges.

allResults.question: A Copilot Studio agent uses a connector to read each employee's own compensation records and submit a correction on that employee's behalf. Which credential design best prevents the maker's permissions from becoming a shared authorization ceiling?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Delegated end-user authorization versus maker identity
allResults.explanation: Microsoft recommends user authentication when a tool retrieves information that only the user can access or performs work on the user's behalf. Agent sign-in and tool credentials are separate settings; a maker-provided connection could let callers exercise the maker's broader authority.

allResults.question: A nightly autonomous agent must read approved invoices from one storage account and create payment-review records in one Dataverse environment. Security policy prohibits stored secrets. What should the architect implement?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Managed identity and least-privilege RBAC
allResults.explanation: An unattended workload needs its own nonhuman identity. Managed identity removes credential storage but grants no permissions by itself, so each dependency still requires the minimum role or application permission at the narrowest practical scope; subscription Owner would create severe excess privilege.

allResults.question: An agent can close customer accounts through a tool that uses a shared service identity. A prompt-injected document causes the model to select another customer's account ID. Which design most directly prevents privilege amplification at execution time?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Tool authorization and privilege amplification
allResults.explanation: The model and retrieved content are not authorization authorities. Sensitive actions must validate structured parameters, ownership, and caller rights outside the model at execution time, with tightly scoped tools and confirmation or approval for high-impact changes. Prompt instructions and content filters cannot enforce business permissions.

allResults.question: A Copilot Studio agent reads regulated case data through a business connector and can send tool output to an arbitrary external HTTP endpoint. The organization also wants each user's source permissions enforced. Which configuration addresses both requirements?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Copilot Studio connector credentials and DLP
allResults.explanation: End-user credentials preserve user-specific downstream permissions, while Power Platform data policies govern which connectors and data paths may coexist. These controls solve different problems: DLP limits exfiltration paths but doesn't provide record authorization, and conversation authentication doesn't choose the tool identity.

allResults.question: A custom RAG agent copies documents from SharePoint sites with different ACLs into one Azure AI Search index. The team proposes retrieving broadly and instructing the model to omit anything the current user should not see. What should the architect require instead?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Grounding security trimming before prompt construction
allResults.explanation: Security trimming must occur during retrieval, before restricted text, metadata, or filenames enter the model prompt. A custom index needs authoritative ACL metadata and a filter built from trusted identity context. Post-generation filtering and model instructions act too late because the unauthorized content has already crossed the boundary.

allResults.question: A platform engineer must configure Foundry networking and deploy models, while a production application only needs to invoke one approved agent. Which authorization design best applies separation of duties?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Foundry control-plane and data-plane authorization
allResults.explanation: Foundry management operations and runtime data operations have distinct authorization surfaces. Microsoft recommends Entra ID with scoped RBAC; an inference-only application should receive a consumer role rather than permissions to configure resources, deploy models, or assign roles. Resource keys grant broad static authority rather than granular per-principal access.

allResults.question: A regulated workload exposes a Foundry model deployment only through a private endpoint. The team plans to remove Entra role checks because the endpoint is no longer reachable from the public internet. What should the architect recommend?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Model endpoint private-network defense in depth
allResults.explanation: Private endpoints reduce network exposure but don't decide which principal may invoke or administer a model. Defense in depth retains Entra ID and scoped RBAC, controls public network access, configures private DNS correctly, and constrains outbound connectivity to approved storage, search, Key Vault, and other dependencies.

allResults.question: A team will fine-tune a support model from transcripts that contain customer identifiers, obsolete access tokens, and internal escalation instructions. Data scientists also currently have permission to deploy any resulting model to production. Which change best protects the lifecycle?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Fine-tuning data and model access separation
allResults.explanation: Service privacy guarantees don't replace customer governance. Training data should be purpose-limited, sanitized of secrets and unnecessary personal data, access-restricted, versioned, and retained only as approved. Separating dataset curation, training, deployment, and invocation prevents one permission from exposing sensitive data or an unapproved custom model.

allResults.question: A Copilot Studio agent passes functional tests using an administrator account, and its automatic security scan reports no blocking issue. Which final release evidence best demonstrates that authorization controls fail closed?
allResults.topic: D3.4 / Negative security testing and authorization auditing
allResults.explanation: A prepublish scan checks important configuration risks but isn't complete security validation. Release testing should include unauthorized and degraded identity cases, inaccessible resources, blocked connectors, and exfiltration attempts, while audit evidence records who attempted which protected operation and why it was allowed or denied without logging secrets.
